titulo: Five things that stop being free once you fly
subtitulo: The health card, a ticket that carries your name, the cash you will actually hand over, and an address that survives a dead phone
cena: Your own kitchen table, ten days out — the last stretch where every one of these is still a five-minute job.
frasePiso: Settled at your own table tonight, none of it turns into a queue in Athens.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: A European health card gets you into the Greek state system, and the gap is specific rather than vague. Inpatient care in the ΕΣΥ is free; outpatient care at ΕΣΥ hospitals and at Κέντρα Υγείας is free. But the patient pays 25 percent of the cost of medicines, one euro per electronic prescription which is never reimbursed, 15 percent for tests at a contracted private provider, and a co-payment at a contracted private hospital. At a private provider that is not contracted, the card covers nothing at all.
fatosDatados.fonte: EHIC/GHIC — a lacuna, bem fonteada (ΕΟΠΥΥ, eu-healthcare.eopyy.gov.gr): internação no ΕΣΥ gratuita; ambulatório do ΕΣΥ e Κέντρα Υγείας gratuitos. Mas: participação de 25% no medicamento; €1,00 por receita eletrônica, não reembolsável; 15% em exames em prestador privado conveniado; coparticipação em hospital privado conveniado; em prestador privado NÃO conveniado o cartão não cobre nada.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: A Greek ferry ticket is nominal by law. The operator registers the name, sex, nationality and date of birth of every passenger — π.δ. 23/1999 as amended by π.δ. 102/2019, transposing EU Directive 2017/2109. Two practical consequences follow directly: you do not buy a ticket for someone else under your own details, and a ticket cannot be passed on to another passenger.
fatosDatados.fonte: Bilhete de balsa é NOMINAL por lei. π.δ. 23/1999, alterado pelo π.δ. 102/2019 (Diretiva UE 2017/2109): registro de nome, sexo, nacionalidade, data de nascimento. Consequência a ensinar: não se compra bilhete para outra pessoa nem se repassa bilhete.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Greece caps what a consumer may hand to a business in notes at 500 euros — article 69 §2 of ν.4446/2016, which cut the earlier ceiling of 1 500 euros. An invoice of 500 euros or more has to be settled by card, transfer or another electronic means.
fatosDatados.fonte: Teto de espécie: €500 para consumidor→empresa — art. 69 §2 do ν.4446/2016, que reduziu o limite anterior de €1.500. Fatura de valor igual ou superior a €500 tem de ser paga por cartão, transferência ou meio eletrônico.

steps.pt: Tonight's list is short and it expires. Five items, all cheaper to settle here than at a counter in Greece.
One: the health card. It buys the state system at resident conditions, and it leaves a known share with you.
Two: any ferry ticket. In Greece it carries a name by law, so book it under the passenger who travels.
Hotel Aigli, good morning.

steps.promptPt: You are ringing the hotel a week before the flight. Open with the job, in one line. Speak now.
steps.es: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση.
steps.pinyin: YA sas, ti-le-fo-NO ya tin KRA-ti-si
steps.pt: Hello, I'm calling about the booking.
steps.tts: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση.

steps.pt: A hotel name is not a destination. A driver and an offline map both want the street and the number.

steps.promptPt: The booking page shows a brand name and a neighbourhood. Get the thing a driver can actually drive to. Speak now.
steps.pt: What is the exact address?
Aristotelous twelve, third floor.

steps.promptPt: You will not hold that in your head, and a tick inside an app is not proof. Ask for it another way. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you write it down for me?
A late arrival is worth saying out loud. Small front desks are not always staffed through the night.

steps.promptPt: Your flight lands at eight and the metro takes an hour. Tell them when to expect you. Speak now.
steps.pt: I arrive at ten at night.

steps.promptPt: Now check that somebody will be standing there when you push the door. Speak now.
steps.es: Είναι ανοιχτή η ρεσεψιόν τη νύχτα;
steps.pinyin: I-ne a-nikh-TI i re-se-PSION ti NI-khta
steps.pt: Is reception open at night?
steps.tts: Είναι ανοιχτή η ρεσεψιόν τη νύχτα;

steps.es: Ναι, η ρεσεψιόν είναι ανοιχτή όλο το εικοσιτετράωρο.
steps.pt: Yes, reception is open around the clock.
steps.tts: Ναι, η ρεσεψιόν είναι ανοιχτή όλο το εικοσιτετράωρο.
steps.acao: Write the answer next to the address, in the same offline note.

steps.pt: Three: cash. Decide the amount now — a single bill of five hundred euros or more cannot be paid in notes.

steps.promptPt: Before you decide how many notes to bring, find out how this place wants to be paid. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you take card?

steps.promptPt: Get something you can dial from someone else's handset if yours arrives flat. Speak now.
steps.es: Ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνο του ξενοδοχείου;
steps.pinyin: pio I-ne to ti-LE-fo-no tu kse-no-dho-KHI-u
steps.pt: What is the hotel's phone number?
steps.tts: Ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνο του ξενοδοχείου;

steps.pt: Four: the ferry office wants the passenger, not the buyer. Every ticket carries a name, and the name is checked.

steps.promptPt: You are booking the island crossing over the phone and the details were read out fast. Check whose crossing it is. Speak now.
steps.es: Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου;
steps.pinyin: to i-si-TI-ri-o I-ne sto O-no-MA mu
steps.pt: Is the ticket in my name?
steps.tts: Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου;

steps.pt: Five: save the address in Greek letters too. Latin spellings vary; the Greek one is what matches the sign.

steps.promptPt: The call did everything you rang for. Close it warmly and finish. Speak now.
steps.pt: Thank you very much. Have a good day.

steps.es: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση. Ποια είναι η ακριβής διεύθυνση; Μπορείτε να μου το γράψετε;
steps.pinyin: YA sas, ti-le-fo-NO ya tin KRA-ti-si. pia I-ne i a-kri-VIS dhi-EF-thin-si. bo-RI-te na mu to GRA-pse-te
steps.pt: Shadow the whole pre-flight call in one run.
steps.tts: Γεια σας, τηλεφωνώ για την κράτηση. Ποια είναι η ακριβής διεύθυνση; Μπορείτε να μου το γράψετε;

steps.pt: B04 done. Card ordered, ticket in your own name, cash decided, address in hand — in both alphabets.

aprofundar.titulo: A list that stops being cheap

secoes.titulo: The health card and the shape of the hole in it
secoes.corpo: A European health card puts you inside the Greek state system on the footing of a resident, and that is worth having. It is also less than most people assume. Inpatient care in the ΕΣΥ is free, and so is outpatient care at ΕΣΥ hospitals and at the Κέντρα Υγείας. From there the shares begin: a quarter of the price of medicines, one euro per electronic prescription that never comes back, fifteen percent on tests at a contracted private provider. At a private provider with no contract, the card does nothing. Order the card early and buy travel insurance as well; they are two different products, not two versions of one.

Greek ferry tickets are nominal by law: name, sex, nationality and date of birth of every passenger, recorded at the point of sale. The rule exists because the operator has to know who is on board. What it means for you is small and absolute — you cannot buy a friend's crossing under your own details, and a spare ticket cannot be given away when plans change. Book each passenger as themselves, with the passport spelling, the first time.

exemplos.es: Το εισιτήριο είναι στο όνομά μου;
exemplos.pt: Is the ticket in my name?

secoes.titulo: How much cash, and why there is a number
secoes.corpo: A consumer may settle a bill in notes only below five hundred euros. From five hundred up, the payment has to go by card, transfer or another electronic route. Almost nothing on a normal trip touches the ceiling, but knowing it exists explains why a large cash payment sometimes produces a question rather than a shrug — and it is the reason a car hire deposit or a week paid up front is a card job, decided before you pack.

secoes.titulo: The address, in the alphabet that is on the sign
secoes.corpo: The Latin version of a Greek street name is what your booking gave you; the Greek version is what is bolted to the corner of the building. Keep both in the same offline note, along with the phone number and the arrival hour. That note is the one thing on this list that works with no signal, no battery on the other side of the conversation, and no shared language.

secoes.titulo: The call is nine short lines
secoes.corpo: None of the Greek here is a document list. It closes the fragile gaps in a booking while a phone call still fixes them for free: confirm it, get the exact address, get it in writing, say what time you land, check that someone is awake.

permissao: You are allowed to over-prepare this one part. Confirming a booking you already hold, or saving an address you will probably never read, is not anxiety — it is the single stretch of the trip where five minutes at your own table buys real cover against a flat battery, a dark doorway and a ticket in the wrong name.
espelho: Anyone who has ever screenshotted a boarding pass in case the airline app hangs is already running this instinct on one document. B04 asks for the same offline habit on four more — the familiar caution, extended, not a new one.

fichasCulturais.sinal: A friend drops out of the island leg and you assume the ferry ticket can simply be used by whoever takes their place.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: It is a boat, not a flight — the ticket is a ticket and nobody is going to check the name on it.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Greek ferry tickets are nominal by law. Name, sex, nationality and date of birth are registered for every passenger, under π.δ. 23/1999 as amended by π.δ. 102/2019, and the manifest is the reason the rule exists at all.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Book each crossing under the passenger who will actually board, spelled as the passport spells it, and treat a change of traveller as a change of ticket rather than a swap.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The name on the ticket matches the name at the gangway, which is the only version of that moment that is not a conversation.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: This is about who the ticket belongs to, not about what a given operator will do at the desk. Refund and rebooking rules are a separate matter and vary by company and by fare.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You arrive expecting the health card to work like insurance, and a share of the bill still turns up at the pharmacy counter.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: The card was refused, or somebody at the desk made a mistake with it.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The card was accepted and did exactly what it is built to do. Hospital care in the state system is free; from there the patient carries defined shares — a quarter of the price of medicines, one euro per electronic prescription, fifteen percent for tests at a contracted private provider.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Carry the card and buy travel insurance as well, and when you have a choice, ask whether the provider is inside the state system before the appointment rather than after it.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The leftover share becomes a small known number instead of a surprise, and the insurance reaches the parts the card was never designed to touch.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a reason to travel without the card. Without it you are outside the state tariff altogether, which is the far more expensive version of the same afternoon.
